Glossary

Plain-language explanations of the technical words marked with a dotted underline on the other pages. The text is the same as the explanation shown there. Only words that a page uses are listed.

Bradford Hill criteria

Nine considerations from 1965 for judging whether a link between two things is likely to be causal, such as strength, consistency and whether the cause comes first.

Also written: Bradford Hill

Used on: Front page, Methods

Canadian Consensus Criteria

A 2003 case definition for ME/CFS. It requires six months of fatigue, worsening after effort, problems with thinking and, in most cases, sleep problems and pain, plus symptoms in other body systems.

Also written: CCC, Canada 2003 criteria

Used on: Fictional hypothesis, Fictional every definition, Second fictional idea, Methods

case definition

A written set of rules (symptoms, how long they have lasted, and illnesses that must be ruled out) used to decide who counts as having ME/CFS in a study.

Also written: case definitions, Case definition

Used on: Front page, Methods

CDC

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the US national public health agency. Its researchers led the 1988 (Holmes) and 1994 (Fukuda) case definitions for chronic fatigue syndrome.

Also written: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

Used on: Fictional every definition, Methods

cohort

A group of people followed or studied together.

Also written: cohorts

Used on: Front page, Fictional hypothesis, Fictional every definition, Second fictional idea, Methods

contested

Marked when a study of comparable or higher quality contradicts the finding behind a rung. An AI auditor decides; no expert has reviewed it. The disputed rung is drawn hatched on the bar.

Also written: Contested

Used on: Front page

control group

People who are compared with the patients, usually healthy people, to see whether a difference is linked to the illness. A study with such a group is called controlled.

Also written: controls, healthy controls, controlled study

Used on: Front page, Fictional hypothesis, Fictional every definition, Second fictional idea

evidence ladder

The six-step scale this site uses to show how much evidence supports a hypothesis, from "Proposed" to "Causal case built". It is a draft.

Also written: ladder

Used on: Front page

Fukuda criteria

A 1994 case definition led by the US CDC. It needs six months of unexplained, disabling fatigue and four of eight listed symptoms. Worsening after effort is one of the eight, but not required.

Also written: Fukuda, Fukuda definition, Fukuda-defined

Used on: Fictional hypothesis, Fictional every definition, Second fictional idea, Methods

Holmes 1988 criteria

The first US CDC case definition for chronic fatigue syndrome (1988). It needs six months of fatigue that halves activity, plus many listed symptoms. Worsening after effort is not required.

Also written: Holmes 1988

Used on: Fictional every definition, Methods

hypotheses

A hypothesis is a proposed explanation that has not been settled. Here, an idea about what causes ME/CFS.

Also written: hypothesis, Hypotheses, Hypothesis

Used on: Front page, Fictional hypothesis, Fictional every definition, Second fictional idea, Methods

International Consensus Criteria

A 2011 case definition for myalgic encephalomyelitis. It requires a marked worsening after effort and symptoms in several body systems, and has no six-month waiting period.

Also written: ICC

Used on: Fictional hypothesis, Fictional every definition, Second fictional idea, Methods

IOM 2015 criteria

A 2015 case definition from the US Institute of Medicine. It requires six months of reduced activity with fatigue, worsening after effort and unrefreshing sleep, plus thinking or standing problems.

Also written: IOM 2015, IOM2015

Used on: Fictional hypothesis, Fictional every definition, Second fictional idea, Methods

long COVID

Health problems that continue or start after a COVID-19 infection and last at least three months. Some of its symptoms overlap with those of ME/CFS.

Also written: Long COVID

Used on: Front page

ME/CFS

Myalgic encephalomyelitis / chronic fatigue syndrome. Severe fatigue that is worse after effort, with unrefreshing sleep. Older papers say CFS or ME; the names came with different case definitions.

Also written: CFS, CFS/ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, chronic fatigue syndrome

Used on: Front page

Oxford criteria

A 1991 UK case definition that requires six months of disabling fatigue and no other specific symptom. It is broad, so a group chosen this way may include people who do not have ME/CFS.

Also written: Oxford definition

Used on: Fictional every definition, Methods

peer-reviewed

Checked by independent experts in the field before a scientific journal publishes it.

Used on: Methods

PEM

Post-exertional malaise. Symptoms get worse after physical or mental effort that was manageable before. It often starts hours to a day or more later and can last days or longer.

Also written: post-exertional malaise

Used on: Front page, Fictional hypothesis, Fictional every definition, Second fictional idea, Methods

preregistered

The plan for a study was filed publicly before it began, saying what would be measured and how it would be analysed. This makes it harder to change the question afterwards.

Also written: preregistration, pre-registered

Used on: Methods

replication

Repeating a study, ideally by a different research group with new patients, to see whether the same result appears. A failed replication is a repeat that does not find it.

Also written: replicate, replicated, replicates

Used on: Fictional hypothesis, Fictional every definition, Methods

The content, including every evidence level, is drafted, checked and decided by AI tools. No medical or research expert has reviewed it. See Methods.

This site describes the state of the evidence. It gives no treatment advice. Built 2026-11-01.
